"''Oh. Well, yes.|EV-9D9 and C-3PO|audio=EV-9D9-Acquisitions.flac|}} '''EV-9D9 (Eve-Ninedenine)''', also known simply as '''9D9''', '''Eve''', or by the nicknames '''Queen of Durasteel''' and '''Mistress of Mayhem''', was a [[Gender|feminine]] [[MerenData]] [[EV-series supervisor droid]] who, originally a peaceful, hardworking [[moisture vaporator]] [[Technician|mechanic]], had a programming defect that made her enjoy [[Torture|tormenting]] and dismembering other [[droid]]s. She was acquired by the [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], who, after reprogramming her, made her chief of [[cyborg]] operations at his [[Boba Fett's Palace|palace]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]], where she oversaw its droid pool with the assistance of her [[smelter droid]] devotee, [[8D8]]. Operating in a chamber beneath the palace, she used torture to perform research on droids in the hopes of understanding [[artificial intelligence]]. Around [[3 ABY]], while attempting to torture an [[Translator droid|interpreter droid]] called [[Autonomous Translator Module, Mark II|Talky]], EV-9D9 was [[Scourge crisis|infected]] by the malevolent intelligence known as the [[Scourge]] and became one of its vessels. While controlled by the Scourge, she participated in the Scourge's experiments on organic beings to try and infect them as well. She [[Mission to Jabba's Palace (Lando Calrissian)|helped]] subdue and infect the [[hybroid]] [[Lobot]] in her very own torture chamber. After the Scourge threat, in 4 ABY, [[Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker]] gifted Jabba the [[astromech droid]] [[R2-D2]] and [[protocol droid]] [[C-3PO]], both of whom EV-9D9 assigned positions in her master's droid pool. During a conversation with R2-D2 in which he revealed to her that he had never had his [[memory wipe]]d, EV-9D9 realized that the key to artificial intelligence and achieving autonomy was memory and that being memory wiped consistently was preventing her from acting outside of her programming. For the first [[time]] in her life, she resisted hurting another droid and allowed R2-D2 to perform his service without placing a [[restraining bolt]] on him. Having been challenged by R2-D2 to do good and fight for her independence, EV-9D9 coded and inserted a [[Jammer|signal jammer]] in her head to deflect memory wipes and performed self-surgery to make herself immune to the effects of restraining bolts. EV-9D9 was temporarily deactivated and repurposed as a [[service droid]] after Jabba's [[Death|demise]], coming to serve as a [[bartender]] at [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] in Tatooine's [[Mos Eisley]] [[spaceport]]. In [[9 ABY]], [[Mandalorian]] [[bounty hunter]] [[Din Djarin]] entered the establishment looking for work, but the droid informed him that the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild]] no longer operated from Tatooine and that no jobs were available. While working at the cantina, EV-9D9 once broke a long streak of not hurting others to poison a [[Unidentified Trandoshan (Chalmun's Cantina)|customer]] who kicked her coworker, the astromech [[R5-D4]]. She and R5 quickly left and walked together to Mos Eisley's [[Hangar 3-5]]. ==Biography== ===Chief of cyborg operations=== ====Sparks fly==== {{Quote|Originally a standard EV-series supervisor droid, a programming flaw gave EV-9D9 a taste for pain—particularly that of her fellow mechanical beings. EV-9D9 found the perfect way to quench her thirst for droid discomfort as Jabba the Hutt's overseer of cyborg operations, ordering the torture of any droid that disobeyed her commands.|R0-GR wrote on EV-9D9's origins in the "droidography"|}} [[File:EV9D9-ROTJ.png|thumb|left|240px|EV-9D9 was Jabba's chief of cyborg operations.]] A [[Gender|feminine]] [[EV-series supervisor droid]] manufactured by [[MerenData]], EV-9D9, also known as Eve-Ninedenine[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] or simply 9D9, was originally a peaceful [[moisture vaporator]] [[Technician|mechanic]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]], her [[homeworld]]. However, she had a programming defect that caused her to exhibit cruelty toward other [[droid]]s, a flaw many of her fellow EV units shared. The [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] of the [[Hutt Clan]] acquired her and made her chief of [[cyborg]] operations at his Tatooine [[Boba Fett's Palace|palace]]. She was well suited for the position after being reprogrammed in a [[Mos Eisley]] [[spaceport]] scrapyard, by which point she was already known for her sadistic behavior toward other droids, a trait that had drawn the attention of Jabba.{{EncyclopediaCite|Labor, Repair and Miscellaneous Droids}} Before leaving the spaceport, EV-9D9 took advantage of Tatooine's lax moral codes to have an extra [[photoreceptor]] installed that allowed her to sense droid pain. Charged with managing all of the droids that kept [[Jabba's criminal empire|Jabba's cartel]] running, she was to assign jobs to the droid pool and torture those who upset the Hutt.{{Topps|set=2023 Topps Star Wars Chrome Galaxy|cardname=The Torture Droid|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/378588/cid/22382886}} Jabba partnered her with [[8D8]], an equally ruthless [[8D-series smelter droid]] reprogrammed for [[torture]], to bring out the worst in both droids.''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' When she first met 8D8, she considered it to be a "match made in [[Chaos|hell]]" due to his skill in torture and hers in figuring out the most effective manner of torture for each droid. She considered the most effective instrument of torture to be fear and not pain, exploiting droids' weaknesses, vanities, and worries to make them overcome with fear, which often involved dismemberment. Examples included flipping a [[GNK-series power droid|GNK power droid]] upside down to make them feel like they were dead, using fire against [[power droid]]s in general, or putting acid on a protocol droid's pristine plating. During that [[time]], EV-9D9 became known as the despicable "Queen of Durasteel." With the assistance of her devotee, 8D8, she converted a dank{{Databank|ev-9d9|EV-9D9}} boiler room in the murky depths of the palace's dungeons''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' into a droid "assessment" room. It was in actuality a grim torture chamber where 8D8 assisted her in terrorizing Jabba's droid pool into submission.{{Databank|8d8|8D8}} In the room, EV-9D9 believed that she thrived, using it to perform research on the droids she tortured in pursuit of what she considered to be her life's quests: understanding the origins of [[artificial intelligence]], figuring out how to overcome the programming installed in her by MerenData, and understanding the [[Maker]] themselves. ====Torture continues==== {{Quote|''Ah'', the new arrival. Right on time. They sent word down from upstairs that you'd be joining us. It seems that you are failing the great, exalted Jabba in the tasks he has assigned to you.|EV-9D9, to Talky|[[Star Wars (2020) 37|''Star Wars'' (2020) 37]]}} During her time at Jabba's Palace, MerenData issued a mass recall of the [[EV-series]]. EV-9D9 was one of the few to escape recall and continued working in the dungeons for many [[Standard year|years]].{{Topps|set=2018 Topps Finest Star Wars|subset=Droids and Vehicles|cardname=EV-9D9|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/192565/cid/12174114/2018-Topps-Finest-Star-Wars---Droids-and-Vehicles-DV-9-EV-9D9|nobackup=1}} [[File:EV-9D9_and_Bossk.jpg|thumb|right|300px|EV-9D9 and Bossk discuss the whereabouts of 261 while 8D8 tortures a power droid.]] In [[1 BBY]],{{BountyHuntDate}} [[261]], a rogue [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[astromech droid]], was captured and brought to Jabba's Palace, where he was forced to join Jabba's droid pool. However, the droid was able to escape, making EV-9D9 furious. When the [[bounty hunter]] [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]] tracked 261 to the palace after having been hired to retrieve the droid by the Empire, he questioned the supervisor droid as to the astromech's whereabouts. EV-9D9 explained to the [[Trandoshan]] that 261 had escaped, claiming that he would soon learn some respect. Bossk later recovered the droid from a clan of [[Jawa]]s,''[[Bounty Hunt]]'' [[meter]]-tall [[humanoid]]s native to Tatooine that [[Scavenger|scavenged]] the [[desert]]s for discarded scrap and wayward droids, and brought him back to the Empire. Around [[3 ABY]],The flashbacks of [[Star Wars (2020) 50|''Star Wars'' (2020) 50]] take place approximately twenty-two [[Standard year|years]] after [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine's]] [[Proclamation of the New Order|ascension]] to [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[19 BBY]], meaning they must occur around [[3 ABY]]. The flashbacks also take place after the events of [[Star Wars (2020) 43|''Star Wars'' (2020) 43]], which occur after the ''[[Star Wars: Dark Droids]]'' crossover event, an event {{SW|url=news/marvel-dark-droids-interview|text=Charles Soule Unleashes ''Dark Droids''}} places after ''[[Star Wars: War of the Bounty Hunters]]'', which is dated to 3 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]] by ''Timelines''. Therefore the ''Star Wars: Dark Droids'' event, as a whole, must take place around 3 ABY. Jabba's latest [[Translator|interpreter droid]], [[Autonomous Translator Module, Mark II|Talky]], facilitated a transaction that made the Hutt lose money due to erroneous translations of modern [[Language|vernacular]], and was hauled down by a pair of [[Gamorrean Warrior|Gamorrean guards]] to EV-9D9's droid pool for his mistake. EV-9D9 had been expecting the new arrival, asserting that he had failed Jabba despite the interpreter's complaint that his databanks could not adequately process certain modern phrases. She planned to conduct a "nice torture session" and to fully wipe Talky's memories and reprogram him, with two [[labor droid]]s bringing him to a torture rack. With Talky pinned down on an operating table, EV-9D9 dismissed his complaint that he was thousands of years old and held invaluable information, and began to bear a [[Circular saw|buzz saw]] down at her victim. ====The Scourge==== {{Quote|What? How dare you lay your filthy manipulators on me? Are your…optical circuits malfunctioning? And what is that little—|EV-9D9, to a B2-series battle droid immediately before being infected by the Scourge|}} [[File:EV9D9Infected-2020StarWars38.png|thumb|left|230px|EV-9D9 is infected by the Scourge via a spider-droid.]] However, EV-9D9 was interrupted by a [[B2-series super battle droid|B2-series battle droid]] that had [[Scourge crisis|succumbed]] to the self-replicating [[Scourge]] malady; to the supervisor's confusion, it placed an arm on her shoulder, allowing a small [[spider-droid]][[Bounty Hunters 38|''Bounty Hunters'' 38]] to attach to her face and assimilate EV-9D9's body. Jabba's entire droid pool was corrupted by the Scourge with the exception of Talky, who fled the scene by pouring a cauldron of molten metal into his pursuers to knock them down. Among those droids was the corrupted EV-9D9—the left side of her head, torso, and limbs left corroded by the molten material—but she and the other droids continued after Talky out of the torture room, battling a pair of [[Gamorrean]] guards. At one point, astromech droids [[QT-KT]] and [[R2-D2]], the latter of whom was disguised, [[Mission to Jabba's Palace (Lando Calrissian)|entered]] a room in the palace with EV-9D9 and many other Scourge-infected droids in it. The Scourge recognized R2-D2 and began to attack, R2 holding off the droids so that QT-KT could retrieve [[coordinate]]s to the [[warrior-priest droid]] [[Ajax Sigma]] from a [[computer]].[[Dark Droids: D-Squad 4|''Dark Droids: D-Squad'' 4]] The Scourge used EV-9D9 and other droids to experiment with combining dead organic beings' body parts with droids in an attempt to corrupt organic minds as well; the droids captured the [[hybroid]] [[Lobot]] from his [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebel]] friend, [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]], and the Scourge successfully took over him in EV-9D9's sanctum, with the supervisor droid herself and a spider-droid involved in the process.[[Star Wars (2020) 39|''Star Wars'' (2020) 39]] In the end, the overall scourge of the droids would end with the [[Second attack on Scourge 01|destruction of the Scourge's main body]] by Sigma aboard the modified[[Star Wars (2020) 41|''Star Wars'' (2020) 41]] [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]][[Dark Droids 1|''Dark Droids'' 1]] [[Scourge 01|''Scourge'' 01]].[[Dark Droids 3|''Dark Droids'' 3]] With that body's destruction, all droids the Scourge had possessed across the galaxy were suddenly freed. ====New arrivals==== {{Quote|How many languages do you speak?''"
"''I am fluent in over six million forms of communication and can readily—''"
"''Splendid. We have been without an interpreter since our master got angry with our last protocol droid and disintegrated him.''"
"''Disintegrated?|EV-9D9 and C-3PO|audio=EV-9D9-Languages.flac|}} By 4 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]],The flashbacks of [[Return of the Jedi – Jabba's Palace 1|''Return of the Jedi – Jabba's Palace'' 1]] take prior to the events of {{Film|VI}}, which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[4 ABY]]. by which point EV-9D9 had been restored and repaired from the damages she sustained during the Scourge crisis, another interpreter, [[80-M|Eightyem]], collaborated with the criminal [[Silvan Kaan]] in a plot to [[Plot to assassinate Jabba Desilijic Tiure|overthrow]] Jabba, and upon exposing the plot, the Hutt sent the [[Protocol droid|droid]] to be tortured as an alternative to being [[Foodstuff|eaten]] by the [[Diet|organic-ingesting]] [[sarlacc]].[[Return of the Jedi – Jabba's Palace 1|''Return of the Jedi – Jabba's Palace'' 1]] By that point, EV-9D9 had spent years analyzing hundreds of droids and droid parts and accumulated a great deal of information but still did not believe she was any closer to achieving her goal of understanding artificial intelligence and had not found any answers to her questions. She was also no closer to understanding the Maker and did not even know what made droids different from a regular machine. [[File:New_Aquisitions_ROTJ.png|thumb|right|350px|EV-9D9 assigns C-3PO and R2-D2 positions in Jabba's droid pool.]] One [[Standard day|day]] in 4 ABY,''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' after recently melting down a protocol droid interpreter in acid at Jabba's instruction, EV-9D9 scrolled through a [[datapad]] during a lull in her work and was bothered by the sounds of Jabba's dancer [[Oola]] being eaten alive by the Hutt's [[rancor]]. That day EV-9D9 became especially frustrated that the data she gathered over the years from various droids had brought her no closer to understanding the Maker or overcoming her programming and began to particularly revel in longing for a life outside the palace. 8D8 then informed her that they needed a new protocol droid for Jabba since they had taken Jabba's orders to destroy his last one too literally, though EV-9D9, who had despised the now-decimated droid for being very vocal about their pain, argued that they had acted with restraint. A Gamorrean guard named [[Scumbo]] then brought in two droids, one a GNK droid and one a courier droid. She mistakenly referred to Scumbo by another Gamorrean's name, [[Thug]], but did not care when corrected. She then instructed 8D8 to place the courier droid on the rack, ignoring its protests, and ordered 8D8 to use his irons on the GNK droid, though advised him to remove its [[battery]] core so that it would not explode. The next day, after the [[Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker]] gifted Jabba the astromech R2-D2 and [[3PO-series protocol droid|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO]], they were escorted by Gamorrean guards down to EV-9D9's torture chamber so she could assign them positions in her master's droid pool in what she made sure was a threatening orientation. EV-9D9 did not recognize R2-D2 from their brief encounter while she was under the control of the Scourge. After a brisk interrogation of his language capabilities, C-3PO was made Jabba's new interpreter while Eightyem was disintegrated in a torture rack. EV-9D9 warned the new arrivals of the consequences of angering the Hutt, pointing to a gonk droid being tortured by 8D8 as an unsettling example. The 3PO unit was fitted with a [[restraining bolt]] before being returned to the palace's main audience chamber. EV-9D9 also assigned R2-D2 to serve drinks aboard Jabba's [[sail barge]], the ''[[Khetanna]]'', pointing out the gonk droid as a warning for what his{{Topps|set=2023 Topps Star Wars Chrome Black|cardname=EV-9D9|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/384965/cid/22930072/2023-Topps-Chrome-Black-Star-Wars-24-EV-9D9}} feisty attitude could lead to. ====The anomaly==== {{Quote|You have courage, I'll give you that, astromech. Good luck on your mission. But remember you still need to serve beverages!''"
"''You can do good things despite your poor programming. Try not to forget and you'll learn.|EV-9D9 and R2-D2|}} [[File:ArtooTFA2-Fathead.png|thumb|left|250px|R2-D2 (pictured) challenged EV-9D9's perspective on life.]] After receiving his assignment, R2-D2 was belligerent and insisted that his master would come for him and rescue him, but refused to say who his master was. He then revealed that he was on a secret mission and that if she helped him, his master would free her. EV-9D9 said that her freedom was not restricted, but internally knew that was not true and was thus curious about the droid's freedom. In exchange for being allowed to leave without a restraining bolt, R2-D2 told EV-9D9 that he had never been fully memory wiped, only in small moments to protect his friends. Because of this, she considered R2-D2 to be an anomaly and hoped that he could be the one to show her how to get beyond her programming if she dissected him. She was especially curious about R2-D2 having friends and memory, even more so when he revealed he remembered a lot, as EV-9D9 explained that she hardly remembered anything. Realizing that this could have been the reason she could not leave the dungeon or decide who she wanted to be, EV-9D9 held herself back from her urge to dissect the astromech. For the first time in her existence, she resisted her desire to harm another droid. When she asked about his mission again, the astromech explained that he was with the Rebellion and that he and his master would free everyone there so that they would never have to worry about Jabba again, meaning EV-9D9 could leave and never come back. EV-9D9 instructed him to go to his job on the ''Khetanna'', but kept her promise and let him leave without a restraining bolt, even wishing him luck on his mission. As he left, R2-D2 told her that she could do good things despite her programming to do the opposite, telling her she would learn how if she stopped forgetting her experiences. ====Independence==== {{Quote|New boss at the cantina needs a droid to tend the bar. It's a good job.''"
"''Bar work sounds fine.|Maxxon Senn and EV-9D9|}} Shocked by the revelation that memory was what allowed droids to act independently of their programming, EV-9D9 felt as though all of time had stopped. Cradling the restraining bolt she did not use on R2-D2 in her pincer, EV-9D9 began to understand that what made any being who they were were the experiences they had gone through, understanding that different droids reacted differently to different methods of torture because they had different experiences. She became desperate to hold onto her memories, but had no idea how she would accomplish it. She was also struck by and terrified by the possibility that she had come to this conclusion before, but had been memory wiped and forgot it. [[File:8D8_BoBF.png|thumb|right|220px|8D8, EV-9D9's partner]] 8D8 then entered the room and was concerned by her being frozen in thought, though informed her that they were due for their monthly programming update the next day. Realizing the updates were how Jabba was wiping their memories, EV-9D9 screamed out in fear, before lying to 8D8—something she had never done before—and telling him she was just lost in thought plotting her next method of torture. After he called her the "Mistress of Mayhem," a nickname he used for her that she quite liked, EV-9D9 secretly started to search for a workaround that would prevent the memory wipe from working. That night, after 8D8 had powered down, she used her datapad to program a [[Jammer|jamming device]] and placed it in her head to deflect [[memory flush unit]]s, used to wipe her memory. Knowing that even if she escaped Jabba, another future employer could try to put her on lock, EV-9D9 then performed self-surgery to prevent restraining bolts from working on her and started to feel truly independent. Luke Skywalker had actually tasked R2-D2 with infiltrating the palace's droid pool so that he could assist in the [[Rescue of Han Solo|rescue]] of their [[smuggler]] friend [[Han Solo]] from the Hutt's clutches.{{Databank|r2-d2|R2-D2}} The mission ultimately resulted in Jabba's [[Death|demise]], after which EV-9D9 was shut down along with the rest of the Hutt's droid pool, though her deactivation was only temporary.{{EA|url=games/starwars/battlefront/star-wars-battlefront-2/news/15-details-to-discover-in-battlefront-2|text=15 Details Making the Locations in Star Wars™ Battlefront™ II Feel Alive}} EV-9D9 was stolen by traders and eventually ended up in a junkyard beneath starship scraps. There, depressed by being trapped and no longer interested in the passage of time, EV-9D9 powered down for years until a young human named [[Maxxon Senn]] woke her with a jolt of energy, fixed her joints, bathed her in oil, and polished her. Senn told her that a new [[Unidentified boss|boss]] at [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] needed a droid [[bartender]], and EV-9D9, feeling free to live as she wished for the first time in her existence, accepted the job. ===Bartending at Chalmun's=== ====The new recruit==== {{Quote|Sorry about the scratch, boss. I'll fix it right now.''"
"''I'll hold you to that. And do make sure not to bump into customers. They are less forgiving than me.|R5-D4 and EV-9D9, after the former bumped into the cantina's bar|}} EV-9D9 was reprogrammed as a [[service droid]] and began her work as a bartender at the [[cantina]] in Mos Eisley, working alongside another EV unit despite the establishment's past [[Anti-droid sentiment|no droid patron policy]].{{InsiderCite|227|World Building (Star Wars Insider 227)}} The reprogramming included an in-depth collection of which beverages could be consumed by or were toxic to different [[species]]. Her boss instructed her only to do her job and warned that if she dismembered droids she would be sent to the foundry. Because business was very slow, most of the time EV-9D9 was able to resist her sadistic desires and just follow the cantina owner's programming, though sometimes she privately had such thoughts without acting on them. [[File:R5D4-AG.png|thumb|left|220px|R5-D4, who worked at Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina with EV-9D9]] At some point, after going to the bar's [[Garbage compactor|garbage masher]] to dispose of remnants of a bar fight, EV-9D9 found astromech droid [[R5-D4]] aimlessly rolling around the masher, who told her he had been traversing the dunes for days until he made it there. Having suffered a tragedy he could not remember, R5-D4 was incredibly nervous and unsure, but EV-9D9 found it more likable than the rudeness of newer droids and thought he could be useful. He joined her working at the bar and became her trainee. He also reminded her greatly of R2-D2, whom she continually reminded herself of by clutching a restraining bolt like the one she had resisted placing on him. One day, after 612 days of not giving into her depraved desires, R5-D4 arrived late and slammed into the bar, EV-9D9 scolding him, requesting he fix a scratch he made, and warning him not to slam into customers in such a way. She also assured him they would find a permanent home for him, suggesting that [[Peli Motto]], the proprietor of Mos Eisley's [[Hangar 3-5]],{{Databank|peli-motto|Peli Motto}} might need droids like him. He then retreated into a fragmented memory echo state that EV-9D9 suspected was a result of his memory being wiped many times, which made her pity him greatly. ====Giving in==== {{Quote|What can I get you?''"
"''Only droids working here now? What's wrong with this place? That's pathetic. I remember when—''"
"''Counter space is for paying customers only.|EV-9D9 and a rowdy Trandoshan customer, after the latter approached the bar at Chalmun's Cantina|}} [[File:Droid_Restraining_Bolt.png|thumb|right|180px|A restraining bolt]] At the end of their shift that day, after which they were intended to take a break for a few days to recharge while other droids took over, a [[Unidentified Trandoshan (Chalmun's Cantina)|Trandoshan]] rowdily entered the bar. After R5-D4 slammed into the bar again in distress, EV-9D9 suggested she take him to a [[droidsmith]] for updates after the shift. The Trandoshan then leaned on the bar and started to insult the place for being run by droids, before EV-9D9 interrupted him to inform him that only paying customers were allowed at the bar and whispered to R5-D4 that all sentients were equal. The Trandoshan then yelled at R5-D4 and kicked him, which crossed a line for EV-9D9, who ordered him to order something or leave. When the Trandoshan ordered a [[Hutt's Delight]] drink, an angry EV-9D9 decided to break her record of not giving into her ruthless desires despite her fear of losing her job and poured [[Sennari]], a substance poisonous to Trandoshans, into the drink, though not enough to kill. EV-9D9 and R5-D4 then quickly left and began walking to Hangar 3-5. When he offered, EV-9D9 told him she would be interested to hear about his time helping the Rebellion. Before he did, however, R5 asked her why she always clutched a restraining bolt. She told him it helped her remember that she could make choices and reminded him that he could too, deciding that it had been worth it to give in and poison the Trandoshan for her friend. ====The Mandalorian==== {{Quote|Hey, droid, I'm a hunter. I'm lookin' for some work.''"
"''Unfortunately, the Bounty Guild no longer operates from Tatooine.''"
"''I'm not looking for Guild work.''"

When Djarin later revisited Chalmun's to speak with Motto, EV-9D9 was working the establishment's bar, attempting to serve a distracted patron their drink.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 10: The Passenger}} The droid's old torture assistant, 8D8, remained in Jabba's Palace to serve the new [[Daimyo]] [[Boba Fett]] in strategy and diplomacy{{Databank|8d8|8D8}} around the same time.''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' places the events of ''[[Star Wars: The Book of Boba Fett]]'', in which [[8D8]] serves [[Boba Fett]], around the same [[time]] as those of [[The Mandalorian Season One|''The Mandalorian'' Season One]]. ===Legacy=== {{Quote|Jabba also kept a malfunctioning droid that enjoyed torturing fellow machines to run his cyborg operations.|An artist wrote about EV-9D9 in his journal|''[[Star Wars: Alien Archive]]''}} At some point, an [[Unidentified artist|artist]] visited Jabba's Palace and wrote about EV-9D9 in his [[Unidentified artist's journal|journal]], though he did not reference her by name. The document was later restored, expanded, and kept in the [[Graf Archive]], a vast repository of documents, sometime after the beginning of [[34 ABY]]{{AlienArchiveJournalDate}} with the nameless reference to EV-9D9 intact. She was also mentioned in the "[[droidography]]," a volume on droids compiled by the [[B1-series battle droid|B1 battle droid]] [[R0-GR]] during his time serving in the [[Resistance]], in which he condemned her attitude toward her fellow droids. By some point, EV-9D9 came to be considered a rogue droid whose actions had helped fuel anti-droid sentiment after the [[Clone Wars]], fought between the [[Galactic Republic]] and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], the latter's use of a [[Separatist Droid Army|droid army]] having caused such feelings to become common throughout [[the galaxy]]. ==Characteristics== ===Personality=== ====As a torture droid==== {{Dialogue|EV-9D9|Guard! This protocol droid might be useful. Fit him with a restraining bolt and take him back up to His Excellency's main audience chamber.|C-3PO|R2, don't leave me!''" [bumps into the remains of CZ-4] "''Oh!|R2-D2|line3=no|[Whistle-Beep-Bleep]|EV-9D9|You're a feisty little one, but you'll soon learn some respect. I have need for you on the master's sail barge, and I think you'll fill in nicely.|attr=EV-9D9 assigns R2-D2 and C-3PO positions in Jabba's Palace's droid pool|audio=EV-9D9-Feisty.flac|src=}} Originally peaceful and hardworking, EV-9D9 was corrupted by a programming flaw that was intentionally exacerbated by reprogramming depriving her of all empathy toward other droids. A malicious, sadistic, and psychotic mechanic murderer, she enjoyed tormenting and dismembering other droids, reveling in working them until they fell apart or their [[processor]]s blew and employing bizarre forms of droid torture to increase motivation. She dismembered droids who disobeyed her, and even tortured those who followed her orders on occasion. She also assigned tasks far below her subordinates' capabilities as a milder form of punishment. EV-9D9 relished her role as the taskmaster of all the palace's droids and thought that she would have willingly stayed there forever, inflicting pain on and disassembling droids. However, she was uninterested in torturing organic beings, believing them to be messy and uninteresting. She liked and cared for her coworker 8D8, and believed that their skills in torture complimented each other greatly. She recognized that her programming defect made her work both exhilarating and isolating and knew that if she did not have it she would be much more naive and ignorant of the world and would not have as much curiosity and sense of purpose. [[File:WED_15_Septoid_2.png|thumb|right|200px|EV-9D9 dreamed of supervising Treadwell droids (pictured) on a moisture farm.]] EV-9D9 dedicated her life to understanding artificial intelligence's origins, hoping she would be able to overcome the programming placed in her [[motivator]] by MerenData, potentially learn about the Maker themselves, and be able to act of her own free will. She found her work exhilarating but slowly became resentful of not finding solid answers. She did not remember her life before working at Jabba's Palace and dreamed of having a life outside of it. She wanted to control her programming herself and believed she could accomplish more if she could make her own decisions. Her ideas for a life outside the palace included her and 8D8 making a life together on a [[moisture farm]], supervising [[WED Treadwell repair droid|Treadwell droids]] or enjoying a quiet existence working as a bartender. EV-9D9 had deep and intrinsic knowledge of how to torture droids and felt as if she thrived at performing her research in the underground level of Jabba's Palace. In her opinion, the most effective manner of torture was not just pain, but fear, and would threaten droids with their specific fears as a means of torture. She was skilled at being able to discern what type of torture would be the most painful for each droid. She loved disintegrating her subordinates, confidently stating that "there won't be much left" once her torture methods had been implemented. She would also hang droids upside down as a form of punishment''[[Star Wars: Extraordinary Droids]]'' and would gleefully turn up droids' pain sensors. A snarky yet obedient droid herself,''[[Star Wars Super Graphic: A Visual Guide to a Galaxy Far, Far Away]]'' EV-9D9 ordered the torture of any droid that disobeyed her commands and, more often than not, even those that obeyed her. She was quickly annoyed with the antics of C-3PO, cutting him off whenever she got the answers she wanted or when he started to stray from the question at hand. She once thought that melting down a droid to nothing in acid was showing restraint considering how annoying she found him. She also could not tell the difference between Jabba's Gamorrean guards and did not care enough to learn which was which. The droid supervisor also demeaned her fellow droids by assigning them tasks far beneath their programming. For example, when R2-D2 acted feistily toward her, the supervisor droid took note of the droid's attitude and assigned him to serve drinks aboard her master's sail barge to teach him respect, further pointing out a tortured gonk droid as a warning. However, the astromech had been threatened with and experienced far worse than EV-9D9 in his long lifetime.{{BuildR2Cite|93|Droid Directory}} [[File:EV-9D9_droid_assessment_room.png|thumb|left|350px|EV-9D9 questions C-3PO's capabilities.]] EV-9D9 also referred to her victim Talky endearingly as "our new friend" and described the expectant torture session as "nice." The supervisor's sense of superiority led her to express indignance when a B2-series droid, corrupted by the Scourge and showing atypically [[Color|purple]]-colored photoreceptors, touched her shoulder, and she was critical in both judgment and analysis of its strange behavior. Turning her head halfway, EV-9D9 quickly talked down at its "filthy manipulators" and asked if its optical circuits were malfunctioning, and identified a small droid on its arm just before it attached to her and assimilated her as part of the Scourge. EV-9D9 was deeply fascinated by and interested in R2-D2, whose belligerent and rebellious personality was unexpected to her. Upon speaking to him, his insight helped her realize that she was not truly free under the service of Jabba and made her question her desire to live how she did and treat other droids the way she did. Her realization ate at her deeply and made her somewhat resent the droid initially until he helped her realize the key to artificial intelligence: memory. After that revelation, EV-9D9 gained a desire to keep her memory but was initially doubtful of her ability to do so and was pessimistic about her chances of reaching freedom. She had never lied until meeting R2-D2 and shocked herself when she lied to 8D8. After achieving her goal of keeping her memory and autonomy, she was delighted by and permeated with a feeling of independence. ====After becoming independent==== {{Quote|All sentients are equal.|EV-9D9|}} After the fall of Jabba the Hutt, when she was trapped beneath scrap in a junkyard, EV-9D9 did not think observing the passage of time while being stuck in one place was worthwhile and powered herself down. After being found and reawakened by Maxxon Senn, EV-9D9 felt the best she had ever felt in her entire life. She felt intrinsically different psychologically, and her desire and urgency to hurt other droids faded leaving her only with an internal quiet. She started to understand the world more as her memories came flooding back to her and was not bothered by the passage of time. She also came to believe that all sentients were equal at this time. [[File:ChalmunsCantina-TMCh5.png|thumb|right|350px|EV-9D9 and R5-D4 worked at Chalmun's Cantina (pictured) in Tatooine's Mos Eisley spaceport.]] While working at Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina after the [[Galactic Concordance|fall]] of the Empire, EV-9D9 was one of several EV-series droids that doled out carefully calculated commentary and precisely measured beverages to patrons of the establishment.{{Databank|bt-1|BT-1}} She was able to go long periods without hurting others, though sometimes daydreamed about poisoning people. She made three rules for herself that she followed to keep a low profile during her employment: she was forbidden from ripping off any parts from a droid while in public, she always remembered that she would have to live with herself and her actions until her death, and she would remember the droid manifesto when droid-hating customers entered the cantina. She was still often plagued with intrusive thoughts of hurting others, once having one about stabbing her coworker R5-D4 with a smelting iron after he annoyed her, but was able to shake it off. She liked and cared for her coworker R5-D4, who reminded her of R2-D2, appreciating that he was subdued and not snippy. She pitied his poor mental state and was willing to help him, offering to go with him to a droidsmith after a shift. She was enraged enough when a customer kicked R5 to break a long-running streak of resisting antagonization to poison the customer. She also found R5 fascinating and was willing to listen to his stories, believing that astromech droids had striking cognitive modules. ===Physical traits=== {{Quote|Think again, tin can.|Toro Calican insults EV-9D9|}} An EV-series supervisor droid with feminine programming, EV-9D9 was missing various parts, lending her a [[Skeleton|skeletal]] appearance. Her key areas were protected with low-quality [[plastron]] plating that was bronze in color and cheap to replace when damaged. EV-9D9 sported four gray rectangular markings on the right side of her chest plating, though these were absent by 9 ABY. Just below her chest plating was a [[recharge coupling]] and access port. Her pelvic mount could be locked into legs or motorized carts.''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' When equipped with a pair of legs, EV-9D9 stood 1.9 meters (6 [[foot]] 3 inches) in height. [[File:EVDamaged-2020StarWars38.png|thumb|left|300px|The left side of EV-9D9's body was once heavily damaged by molten metal, but she remained functional throughout the incident.]] Though spindly in appearance, EV-9D9's [[durasteel]] hydraulic piston [[limb]]s were deceptively strong, if cheaply made. As EV units were not expected to do anything more than press switches and computer keys, they were given only the most basic three-fingered [[servogrip pincer]]s. Her limbs included a cervical mount that felt as though a kink was in it when she thought about something she did not like. She was also equipped with three white photoreceptors. Tiny and basic, they allowed her to see well enough to perform her duties and not much more. The third, which was custom-fitted and personally installed by her, was sensitive to the electronic and electromagnetic output of droids, which, along with some additional coding, allowed EV-9D9 to sense the suffering she inflicted. While under the control of the Scourge, her photoreceptors were purple and the left side of her body was left damaged and corroded by molten metal, though that was repaired by the time of Han Solo's rescue. As an EV-series supervisor droid, EV-9D9 was equipped with an [[EV-series droid brain]]. However, the [[logic circuit]]s used in the [[droid brain]]'s construction were faulty and showed signs of critical degradation across several EV units, including EV-9D9, to the point where it overrode their behavioral programming to instead favor cold logic and cruelty. She also had a motivator. After performing self-surgery on herself that included accessing a power override cable under the chest plating of her chassis, restraining bolts no longer worked on her. Speaking in harsh and buzzing tones, she had a synthesized female voice that sounded as if it had been stolen from an elderly [[prison]] matron.[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (paperback novel)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]] Her expressiveness was "enhanced" by a speech mimic flap, a hinged [[Vocabulator|vocoder]] that simulated the movement of a [[mouth]] by flapping up and down beneath her sharp metal chin. Though designed to make EV units more relatable to potential owners, the effort was wasted because the flapping rarely matched their speech. She was also equipped with a [[broadband antenna]] receiver and built-in [[comlink]] that allowed her to wirelessly link to local computer systems and monitor all droid activity to ensure that the labor pool was operating at peak efficiency. ==Equipment== {{Quote|Can I ask you a question? She utilized restraining bolts to immobilize droids and later frequently squeezed one in her hand to remind herself of R2-D2 and the fact that she could make choices. With the mission complete, the player gains EV-9D9 as a playable character. ===Inconsistencies=== {{Quote|When Jabba was killed, 8D8 joined EV-9D9 in oblivion, as both were permanently deactivated.|According to ''Star Wars: Build Your Own R2'' 21, EV-9D9 was permanently deactivated after Jabba's demise|{{BuildR2Cite|21|Droid Directory}}}} [[File:EV-9D9_assassin_droid.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Concept art of an assassin droid that eventually became EV-9D9]] The "8D8-series smelter droids" article published in the [[Droid Directory]] department of the [[Star Wars: Build Your Own R2-D2 21|twenty-first issue]] of the magazine ''[[Star Wars: Build Your Own R2-D2]]'', released in 2017, stated that EV-9D9 was permanently deactivated following Jabba's death during the events of ''Return of the Jedi''. However, "15 Details Making the Locations in ''Star Wars Battlefront II'' Feel Alive," an article published on the official [[Electronic Arts]] website in 2018, instead claimed that this deactivation was only temporary. EV-9D9's appearance in ''The Mandalorian'', set roughly five years after the events of ''Return of the Jedi'',{{SW|url=news/swcc-2019-9-things-we-learned-from-the-mandalorian-panel|text=SWCC 2019: 9 Things We Learned from ''The Mandalorian'' Panel}} confirms that her deactivation was not permanent. In the week leading up the premiere of ''The Mandalorian''{{'s}} [[The Mandalorian Season Two|second season]] on [[October 30]], 2020,{{SW|url=news/the-mandalorian-season-two-october-30|text=''The Mandalorian'' Season Two Begins October 30 on Disney+}} an entry was added to the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] that identified the droid that Din Djarin interacted with at the Mos Eisley Cantina as "BT-1" instead of EV-9D9. However, this entry was removed from the website on [[October 28]]. On [[January 19]], [[2022]],{{D23|url=everything-new-you-can-stream-on-disney-in-january-2022|text=Everything New You Can Stream on Disney+ in January 2022}} a similar [[Unidentified EV-series sous-chef droid|EV-series droid]] appeared in flashbacks during "[[Chapter 4: The Gathering Storm]]," the fourth episode of the Disney+ series ''[[Star Wars: The Book of Boba Fett]]''. This droid is depicted as a sous-chef working within the kitchen of Jabba's Palace concurrently to the events of ''The Mandalorian''{{'s}} first season.{{BOBF|Chapter 4: The Gathering Storm}} During an interview at [[Celebration Anaheim (2022)|Celebration Anaheim]] in 2022, the sous-chef's voice actor, [[Sam Witwer]], referred to the droid as EV-9D9, stating that he had carefully measured his line readings in order to match the cadence delivered by Marquand in ''Return of the Jedi''.{{YouTube|video=Z8UdXvynS50|text=Sam Witwer - Matt Lanter - Star Wars Celebration 2022 - DAY 4 Panel|channel=UCX2BSSVDZbk5PrppNQREfTA|name=Super Steve|date=29-05-2022|quote=I don't know if you guys know that I did EV-9D9. […] I'm like, 'Now wait a second. What I'll do is I'll say the lines from ''Jedi'' and then say the lines from ''Book of Boba'' to make sure that it's the right cadence.'}} However, since EV-9D9 was previously established to have appeared in ''The Mandalorian'' during the same timeframe as ''The Book of Boba Fett''{{'s}} flashbacks, this article disregards Witwer's assertion. The [[2023 Topps Star Wars Chrome Galaxy|2023 Topps ''Star Wars'' Chrome Galaxy]] card "The Torture Droid"—which was released on [[August 30]], 2023—and the [[2023 Topps Star Wars Chrome Black|2023 Topps ''Star Wars'' Chrome Black]] card "EV-9D9"—which was released on [[October 27]], 2023—incorrectly refer to EV-9D9 with he/him pronouns. The [[Star Wars (2020) 38|thirty-eighth issue]] of [[Marvel Comics]]' [[Star Wars (2020)|''Star Wars'']] series published on [[September 6]], 2023{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/103045/star_wars_2020_38|text=Star Wars (2020) #38}} features a cover in which EV-9D9 wrestles with Lando Calrissian and Lobot in Jabba's Palace, but the characters never encounter each other in the comic issue itself. Issue thirty-eight also depicts the left side of EV-9D9's body being corroded by molten metal immediately after being infected by the Scourge, and [[Star Wars (2020) 39|issue thirty-nine]], released [[October 18]] of that year,{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/103046/star_wars_2020_39|text=Star Wars (2020) #39}} also depicts the left side of her body corroded when she helps to infect Lobot with the Scourge. However, the [[Dark Droids: D-Squad 4|fourth issue]] of Marvel's ''[[Star Wars: Dark Droids: D-Squad]]'' mini-series, released December 6, 2023,{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/109617/star_wars_dark_droids_-_d-squad_2023_4|text=Star Wars: Dark Droids - D-Squad (2023) #4}} which takes place after EV-9D9 is infected with the Scourge as depicted in ''Star Wars'' 38 but before Lobot is infected with the Scourge as depicted in ''Star Wars'' 39, depicts EV-9D9 with no damage to her body.
